meta.title: My English Book
meta.subtitle: Pupil's Book · Class 1
insideCover: Write your name on this page. Draw a sun and colour it yellow.
If you find this book, please return it to the school.
howToUse: One unit takes about two weeks: two or three short lessons of 30 minutes.
Each unit has the same steps: Listen and say · New words · Talk with a friend · Say it together · Do it · Check yourself.
Do not write in the book if the school re-uses copies — say the answers aloud, or use an exercise book.
The teacher's notes for every unit are in the Class 1 Teacher's Guide (same theme order).
Read the story at the end of each unit aloud. Pupils join in with the repeated line.
songLines: I am fine, I am fine,
I am fine, I am fine,

themes.title: Hello, My Family
themes.blurb: At home with Mother, Father, Grandmother and the baby. We greet people, say our name, talk about our family, count to five and learn nine colours.

units.title: Hello! Good Morning
units.competence: To greet people at home and at school, to say my name and to ask someone else's name.
units.caption: Bih and Ngo greet their teacher at the school gate.

listen.instructions: Listen to your teacher. Then say the words with your teacher.
lines: Teacher: Good morning, children.
Pupils: Good morning, teacher.
Teacher: Good morning, Bih. How are you?
Bih: I am fine, thank you.
Teacher: Good morning, Ngo.
Ngo: Good morning, teacher. I am fine.

talk.instructions: Stand in a circle. Greet the child on your right. Say your name. Then listen to your friend's name.

practice.instructions: Match. Draw a line from the English word to the French word.
Trace the words. Start at the dot. Say the word as you trace it.
Complete the conversation with your teacher. Fill in the gaps.
lines: A: Good _____, Aisha.
B: Good _____, Bih. How are _____?
A: I am _____, thank you.

practice.instructions: Say the right greeting. Your teacher will say the time of day.

units.challenge: Work with a friend. One of you is the teacher, the other is a new pupil. Greet and say your names. Then swap.

song.title: Song: Good Morning
lines: Good morning, good morning,
How are you today?
I am fine, I am fine,
Thank you very much!

story.title: Story: The New Girl
lines: It is the first day of school. Ngo is new.
She stands at the gate. She feels shy.
A girl comes to her. "Hello! Can I play with you?" asks Bih.
"Yes!" says Ngo.
Ngo says, "Good morning. My name is Ngo."
Bih says, "Good morning, Ngo. My name is Bih."
Now they are two good friends.
They walk to the classroom together.

check: I can greet somebody in the morning.
I can say my name.
I can ask a friend's name.
I know these words in English: hello, goodbye, name.
units.homework: Greet three people at home in English this evening. Say: "Good evening!" Ask them their name in English.

units.title: My Family
units.competence: To name the people in my family and to say who I live with.
units.caption: This is my family. We live together in our home.

listen.instructions: Listen to the teacher. Then repeat each line. Show the person on the picture.
lines: This is my family. We live in our home.
This is my mother. She cooks every day.
This is my father. He works in the field.
This is my grandmother. She tells us stories.
This is my baby sister. She sleeps in the afternoon.
My family loves me. I love my family.

talk.instructions: Show your family to your friend. Say who they are. Ask your friend about their family.

practice.instructions: Look at the picture of the family. Say the words. Write the missing letter in each word.
lines: m_th_r
f_th_r
gr_ndmoth_r
b_by
br_th_r
s_st_r

practice.instructions: Circle the right word.
lines: My ______ cooks the food. (mother / father)
My ______ tells us stories before bed. (grandmother / baby)
My ______ is very small. He cannot walk. (baby / grandfather)

practice.instructions: Talk. Sit with a friend. Look at the picture. Tick what you can see.
Draw your family in the box with your crayon. Then say: "This is my ______."
practice.caption: My family

units.challenge: Play "Who is it?". One pupil says: "My father's mother." The others answer: "Grandmother!"

song.title: Song: Finger Family
lines: Mother finger, mother finger, where are you?
Here I am, here I am, how do you do?
Father finger, father finger, where are you?
Here I am, here I am, how do you do?

story.title: Story: The Pot of Beans
lines: Mother cooks beans. The pot smells sweet.
Baby cries. "Ay, ay, ay!"
Grandmother carries the baby. She sings to the baby.
Father brings water from the tap.
Bih sets the plates. Ngo brings the spoons.
Everyone sits on the mat. The family eats together.
Mother says: "Thank you, my children. We eat together."
The beans are sweet. The family is happy.
story.say: This is my family. We eat together.

check: I can name six people in my family.
I can say who I live with.
I can ask "Who is this?"
I listen to my friend when they speak.
units.homework: Ask your mother or grandmother the names of your family in English. Draw one person from your family in your exercise book and label it.

units.title: One, Two, Three — Count!
units.competence: To count from 1 to 10 and to say how many things are in a group.
units.caption: Count the things. How many?

listen.instructions: Listen and point. Say the number after your teacher.
lines: one ball
two bananas
three mangoes
four chickens
five paw-paws
six books
seven stones
eight leaves
nine spoons
ten fingers

talk.instructions: Pick up some stones. Put them on the table. Your friend counts them in English.
questions: How many fingers do you have?

practice.instructions: Count and write the number word. Use the word bank.
Count the picture. Circle the right number.
lines: In the picture there are ______ chickens. (four / six)
There are ______ mangoes. (three / five)
There are ______ paw-paws. (two / five)

practice.instructions: Trace the numbers. Say them in English.
Join the number to the right group of dots.

units.challenge: Count the number of chairs, doors and windows in your classroom. Say: "There are three windows."

song.title: Song: Ten Little Fingers
lines: One little, two little, three little fingers,
Four little, five little, six little fingers,
Seven little, eight little, nine little fingers,
Ten little fingers on my hands!

story.title: Story: The Market Basket
lines: Mother gives Bih a basket. "Go to the market, please."
Bih buys one paw-paw. "One paw-paw, please."
Bih buys two bananas. "Two bananas, please."
Bih buys three mangoes. "Three mangoes, please."
Bih buys four tomatoes. "Four tomatoes, please."
Bih buys five fish. "Five fish, please."
Ngo counts in the basket: "One, two, three, four, five!"
Mother smiles. "Very good, Bih. You can count!"
story.say: One paw-paw, two bananas, three mangoes…

check: I can count from 1 to 10 in English.
I can say "How many?"
I can count things in the classroom.
I can write the numbers 1 to 5.
units.homework: Count ten things at home in English: plates, cups, chairs, stones. Say: "There are four plates."

units.title: Colours All Around
units.competence: To name nine colours and to say the colour of an object.
units.caption: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, brown, black and white.

listen.instructions: Listen and find. Your teacher says a colour. Point to something in the room that colour.
lines: This is red. Like a football.
This is green. Like a leaf of the plantain.
This is yellow. Like a paw-paw.
This is orange. Like an orange.
This is brown. Like the earth in the road.
This is blue. Like the sky at midday.
Red, yellow and green are our flag colours in Cameroon.
The star on our flag is yellow.
Black and white. Like the shirts of school.

talk.instructions: Look at your clothes. Tell your friend the colour. Ask about their clothes.

practice.instructions: Colour the ball red, the leaf green, the sun yellow. Say the sentence aloud.
practice.caption: Colour the pictures

practice.instructions: Match the word to the colour.
Fill in the colour words.
lines: The paw-paw is ______.
The leaf is ______.
The ball is ______.
The chalk is ______ .

practice.instructions: Tick the colours of the Cameroon flag. Then say: "The flag is green, red and yellow."

units.challenge: Play "Colour hunt". Your teacher says a colour. In one minute, find and touch three things of that colour.

song.title: Song: Rainbow Song
lines: Red and yellow and pink and green,
Purple and orange and blue;
I can sing a rainbow, sing a rainbow,
Sing a rainbow too.

story.title: Story: Ngo's New Dress
lines: Grandmother brings cloth from the market.
It is green and red and yellow.
They are the colours of our flag.
Grandmother sews a dress for Ngo.
"What colour is your dress?" asks Bih.
"It is green, red and yellow!" says Ngo.
Ngo dances in the yard. The dress spins like a flower.
"You are beautiful, Ngo," says Grandmother. Ngo is very happy.
story.say: The dress is green, red and yellow.

check: I can name nine colours.
I can say the colour of something.
I know the colours of the Cameroon flag.
I can colour inside the lines.
units.homework: Find five things at home with different colours. Say: "The cup is white." Draw them in your exercise book and colour them.

themes.title: My Village, My Town
themes.blurb: In the village and in the town. We go to the market, name animals, and learn to ask for things politely.

units.title: My Home, My House
units.competence: To name the rooms and things in a home and to say what happens in each place.
units.caption: This is my house. We sleep, cook and eat here.

listen.instructions: Listen and point to the picture. Say each word after your teacher.
lines: This is my house. It has a roof and a door.
This is the room. We sleep in the room. There is a mosquito net.
This is the kitchen. Mother cooks in the kitchen.
There is a pot on the fire. There is water in the jerrycan.
We eat on the mat. We put food on the plate.
There is a cup for water. There is a broom for the floor.
We keep the house clean. Every day.

talk.instructions: Draw your house with your finger in the air. Tell your friend: what is in it?

practice.instructions: Label the picture. Use the word bank.
Match the action to the place or thing.
Complete the sentences.
lines: Mother cooks in the ______.
I sleep on the ______.
We drink water from a ______.

practice.instructions: Tick what you can see in the picture.

units.challenge: In groups, tell the class one thing you do in your house every morning. Say: "I sweep the floor."

song.title: Song: This Is My House
lines: This is my house, this is my home,
Here I cook and here I sleep,
This is my house, this is my home,
Keep it clean and keep it neat!

story.title: Story: Clean the House
lines: It is Saturday. The sun is hot.
Mother says: "Children, let us clean the house."
Bih sweeps the floor. The broom is tall.
Ngo washes the plates in a basin.
Father carries water in a jerrycan.
Grandmother puts the mats in the sun.
The house is clean and sweet.
Mother says: "Thank you, my children. A clean house is a happy house."
story.say: A clean house is a happy house.

check: I can name things in my house.
I can say where I sleep and eat.
I can say one way to keep my house clean.
I say my words clearly.
units.homework: Draw your house in your exercise book. Label three things in English: door, plate, bed.

units.title: At the Market
units.competence: To ask for things politely at the market and to name the people and things we find there.
units.caption: This is the market. We buy and sell food here.

listen.instructions: Listen to the market talk. Then repeat with your teacher.
lines: This is the market. It is very busy.
The market woman sells tomatoes and plantains.
Bih has money. Ngo has a basket.
Bih says: "Good morning, madam."
The woman says: "Good morning, my child."
Bih says: "Two tomatoes, please."
The woman says: "Here you are."
Bih says: "Thank you!"

talk.instructions: One pupil is the market woman. One pupil is the buyer. Buy and sell. Be polite!

practice.instructions: Put the conversation in the right order. Write 1 to 4.
lines: ______ "Here you are."
______ "Good morning, madam."
______ "Thank you!"
______ "Two tomatoes, please."

practice.instructions: Match the word and the picture description.
right: We swim in water. We are food.
It is hot and small and red.

practice.instructions: Complete with the polite words.
lines: A: Three mangoes, ______.
B: Here you are.

practice.instructions: Tick the things you can buy at the market.

units.challenge: Make a market corner in your classroom. Bring clean empty packets. Sell and buy in English, using please and thank you.

song.title: Chant: Market Chant
lines: Tomato, tomato, two tomatoes please!
Plantain, plantain, one plantain please!
Thank you, madam, thank you, sir!
Money in the market, basket in my hand!

story.title: Story: The Spilled Basket
lines: Ngo goes to the market with Mother.
Ngo carries a basket of tomatoes.
A boy runs past. Bump! The basket falls.
Oh no! The tomatoes roll in the dust.
Ngo wants to cry. Her eyes are wet.
The market woman comes. She helps Ngo.
They pick up every tomato and clean them.
"Thank you, madam," says Ngo. "You are very kind."
story.say: Thank you, madam. You are very kind.

check: I can name five things at the market.
I can ask for something with "please".
I can say "thank you".
I can buy and sell in a game.
units.homework: At home, ask politely in English: "Water, please." and say "Thank you." Practise three times.

units.title: In the Village, In the Town
units.competence: To talk about where I live and to name things I see in the village and in the town.
units.caption: Some of us live in a village. Some of us live in a town.

listen.instructions: Listen to Ngo and Bih. Then say where you live.
lines: Ngo lives in a village. Her village is small.
There are many trees and a river.
There are farms and goats and hens.
Bih lives in a town. Her town is big.
There are many cars, shops and a hospital.
In the village and in the town, there is a school.
We all go to school. We all learn English.

talk.instructions: Tell your friend: "I live in a village" or "I live in a town." Then say two things you see there.

practice.instructions: Tick. Is it in a village, a town, or both?
Match the opposites.
Complete the sentences.
lines: My village is ______. (small / many)
There is a ______ near my house. (river / plate)
We go to ______ every day. (school / field)

practice.instructions: Draw where you live. Draw two things you see there. Say: "This is my ______."
practice.caption: Where I live

units.challenge: Work in pairs. One pupil comes from the village, one from the town. Say three things that are the same where you live.

song.title: Chant: My Home Place
lines: Village, village, trees so tall,
Town, town, shops and all,
River, road and school and sun,
Cameroon is home for everyone!

story.title: Story: Ngo Visits the Town
lines: Ngo lives in a small village. She visits Bih in the town.
Ngo sees a big road. She sees many cars.
"Oh! The cars are so fast!" says Ngo.
Ngo sees a big shop. She sees a hospital.
"In my village we have one small shop," says Ngo.
Bih says: "In your village you have a big river and many trees."
"Yes," says Ngo. "And you have mangoes?"
"No," says Bih. "Come and play. We can share."
story.say: Where do you live? I live in a ______.

check: I can say where I live.
I can name five things in my village or town.
I can say "big" and "small".
I listen when my friend tells about their home.
units.homework: Ask your mother or father: "Where did you live when you were small?" Then draw one thing they tell you about.

units.title: Animals Around Us
units.competence: To name animals near our homes and to say the sound each animal makes.
units.caption: We have animals at home and in the bush.

listen.instructions: Listen to the animals. Make the sound with your teacher.
lines: This is a hen. The hen says "kot, kot, kot".
This is a goat. The goat says "meh, meh".
This is a dog. The dog says "wouf, wouf".
This is a cat. The cat says "miaou".
This is a cow. The cow is big. It says "moo".
This is a bird. The bird is small. It flies in the sky.
The monkey and the elephant live in the bush.
Which animal do you like?

talk.instructions: Choose one animal. Say: "I like the ______. It says ______." Your friend guesses the animal.

practice.instructions: Match the animal to its home or what it gives us.
Write the animal. Use the word bank.
lines: "Wouf, wouf" = ______

practice.instructions: Tick big or small.
Draw your favourite animal. Say: "This is a ______."
practice.caption: My favourite animal

units.challenge: Play animal sounds. One pupil makes a sound. The others say the English name of the animal.

song.title: Song: Old MacDonald
lines: Old MacDonald had a farm, E-I-E-I-O,
And on his farm he had a hen, E-I-E-I-O,
With a kot-kot here and a kot-kot there,
Here a kot, there a kot, everywhere a kot-kot!

story.title: Story: The Clever Hen
lines: A hen lives near the house. She has five chicks.
A big dog comes near. The chicks are afraid.
The hen opens her wings wide. "Kot, kot, kot!"
The chicks hide under her wings.
The dog looks and looks. He cannot see the chicks.
The dog goes away.
The hen is clever. She protects her chicks.
"Kot, kot, kot!" says the hen. The chicks are safe.
story.say: The hen is clever. She protects her chicks.

check: I can name eight animals.
I can say the sound of a hen, a goat and a dog.
I can say "big" and "small".
I can say which animal I like.
units.homework: Watch the animals near your home. Count the hens you see. Say in English: "I see four hens."

themes.title: My School
themes.blurb: In our classroom. We learn about jobs, we find out where people are, and we take care when we travel.

units.title: People and Jobs
units.competence: To name people's jobs and to say what a person does.
units.caption: Who helps us? The nurse, the teacher, the carpenter.

listen.instructions: Listen. Then point to each person in the picture.
lines: This is a teacher. The teacher teaches us to read.
This is a nurse. The nurse helps us at the hospital.
This is a farmer. The farmer grows maize and cassava.
This is a carpenter. The carpenter makes tables and chairs.
This is a driver. The driver drives the bus to Douala.
This is a market woman. She sells tomatoes and plantains.
They all work. They all help us. Say thank you often.

talk.instructions: Act a job. Do not speak! Your friends guess in English: "You are a ______."
questions: What work do you want to do?

practice.instructions: Match the person to what they do.
Complete the sentences.
lines: The ______ drives the bus.
The ______ sells tomatoes.
The ______ helps me when I am sick.
The ______ teaches me English.

practice.instructions: Tick the people who work in a hospital.
Draw the work you want to do when you are big. Say: "I want to be a ______."
practice.caption: My work when I am big

units.challenge: Invite a nurse or a farmer to talk to your class. Prepare two questions in English: "What is your work?" "Do you like your work?"

song.title: Chant: The Helper Chant
lines: The farmer grows, the carpenter builds,
The teacher teaches, the nurse gives pills;
The driver drives, the seller sells,
We thank them all, our helpers!

story.title: Story: Nurse Mary Visits
lines: Nurse Mary comes to visit the class.
She wears a white uniform. She carries a small bag.
"Do you wash your hands?" she asks.
"Yes!" shout the pupils.
"When do you wash your hands?"
Bih says: "Before we eat."
Ngo says: "After the toilet."
"Very good," says Nurse Mary. "Clean hands keep us well."
All the class wash their hands together.

check: I can name six jobs.
I can say what a person does.
I can ask "What is your work?"
I can say "thank you" to people who help us.
units.homework: Ask two adults at home about their work. Draw one of them working and say: "This is a ______."

units.title: Up, Down, Here, There
units.competence: To say where a thing or a person is.
units.caption: The bus is on the road. The mother is in the taxi park.

listen.instructions: Listen and put your hand where the teacher says.
lines: Where is the book? The book is on the table.
Where is the bag? The bag is under the chair.
Where is the teacher? The teacher is next to the door.
Where is the ball? The ball is in the basket.
Here is a pencil. There is a window.
Where is the bus? The bus is on the road.

talk.instructions: Hide a small stone in the classroom. Your friend asks: "Where is the stone?" Answer: "It is on the chair."
questions: It is in / on / under the ______.

practice.instructions: Look at the picture. Complete the sentences with in, on, under or next to.
lines: The bag is ______ the chair.
The taxi is ______ the road.
The mother is ______ the bus stop.
The boy is ______ the basket.

practice.instructions: Draw. The cat is under the table. The cup is on the table. The ball is next to the bag.
practice.caption: Where are the things?

practice.instructions: Match the question to the answer.
Tick the correct sentence.
rows: The bag is under the chair.
The hen is on the mat.

units.challenge: Put five things in different places in the classroom. Say where each one is. A friend finds them.

song.title: Song: Where Is It?
lines: Where is the ball? Where is the ball?
On the chair, under the table, next to the door!
Here it is! There it is!
Now let's count: one, two, three, four!

story.title: Story: The Missing Shoe
lines: It is morning. Bih cannot find her shoe.
"Mother, where is my shoe?" she asks.
"Look under the bed," says Mother.
Bih looks under the bed. No shoe.
"Look on the chair," says Ngo.
Bih looks on the chair. No shoe.
"Look in the bag!" says Grandmother.
Bih opens the bag. The shoe is in the bag!
"Thank you, Grandmother!" says Bih. Now she runs to school.
story.say: Where is my shoe? It is in the bag.

check: I can say in, on, under, next to.
I can ask "Where is it?"
I can say where things are in my classroom.
I help my friend to find things.
units.homework: Put three things in different places at home. Ask your brother or sister: "Where is the ______?" and answer in English.

units.title: Food and Water
units.competence: To name common foods and to say what we must do to stay healthy.
units.caption: We eat rice, beans, plantains and fruit. We drink clean water.

listen.instructions: Listen. Then say the sentences with your teacher.
lines: We eat rice and beans. This food is good for us.
We eat plantains, ndolé and koki. They are Cameroonian food.
We eat fruit: mango, paw-paw, banana and orange.
We drink water every day. Clean water is good.
We wash our hands with soap before we eat.
We wash fruit before we eat it.
We cook meat and fish very well. Then we are strong and well.

talk.instructions: Say what you ate this morning. Say what you like. Then ask your friend.
questions: Yes, I like it. / No, thank you.

practice.instructions: Match the food to the colour.
Put a ✔ for good and a ✘ for not good.
Complete the sentences.
lines: I eat ______ for lunch.
I drink ______ every day.
Before I eat I wash my ______ with ______.

practice.instructions: Draw your favourite food. Say: "I like ______. It is good for me."
practice.caption: My favourite food

units.challenge: Work in groups. Make a healthy plate. Draw rice, beans, plantain and fruit. Then tell the class: "This is good food."

song.title: Song: Wash Your Hands
lines: Wash, wash, wash your hands,
Wash them with soap and water!
Before you eat, after the toilet,
Wash, wash, wash your hands!

story.title: Story: The Mango Tree
lines: There is a mango tree near the school.
The mangoes are yellow and sweet. The children love them.
Ngo picks one big mango. She starts to eat.
"Stop!" says Bih. "Did you wash it?"
"No," says Ngo. "But it is from the tree!"
"Our teacher says wash it first. There is dust and flies on it."
Ngo washes the mango in clean water.
Then she eats it. It is very sweet and she is safe.
"Thank you, Bih," says Ngo.

check: I can name six foods.
I can say what I like to eat.
I know to wash my hands before I eat.
I know to wash fruit in clean water.
units.homework: Help to wash fruit or vegetables at home. Say in English: "I wash the mango. It is clean."

units.title: My Body — Keep It Safe
units.competence: To name the parts of my body and to say how I keep my body safe and clean.
units.caption: This is my body. I keep it clean and safe.

listen.instructions: Listen and touch the part of your body with your hand.
lines: This is my head. I wash my head.
These are my eyes. I use my eyes to see.
These are my ears. I use my ears to listen.
This is my nose. I smell food with my nose.
This is my mouth. I brush my teeth every morning.
These are my hands. I wash my hands with soap.
These are my feet. I wear shoes to protect my feet.
I keep my body clean. I keep my body safe.

talk.instructions: Play "Simon says". Your teacher says: "Simon says touch your nose." Do it. If the teacher does not say "Simon says", do not move!
questions: What do you do with your ears?

practice.instructions: Match the body part to its work.
Label the body. Use the word bank.
Tick what keeps you safe and clean.
rows: Walk on the road where cars go fast.
Put your hand on a hot pot.

practice.instructions: Draw a face. Draw the eyes, the nose and the mouth. Say what each part is for.
practice.caption: My face

units.challenge: Make a health poster for the class. Draw a hand with soap. Write or copy: "Wash your hands!"

song.title: Song: Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes
lines: Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes,
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes,
And eyes and ears and mouth and nose,
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes!

story.title: Story: The Broken Tap
lines: The tap at school is broken. There is no water.
The children cannot wash their hands.
"What can we do?" asks Ngo.
Bih has an idea. "Let us bring water from home."
The children bring water in small jerrycans.
They put soap next to the basin.
Now everybody can wash their hands.
The teacher says: "Well done, children. You keep us safe."
story.say: Wash your hands. Keep your body clean and safe.

check: I can name nine parts of my body.
I can say what my eyes and ears do.
I can say how I keep my body clean.
I can play "Simon says" in English.
units.homework: Show your family the song "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes". Sing it in English and do the actions.

usefulSentences: How are you? — I am fine, thank you.
Comment vas-tu ? — Je vais bien, merci.
What is this? — It is a ______.
Where is the ______? — It is on the table.
Où est le ______ ? — Il est sur la table.
